b2-30-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Cafés
b2-30-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks which café is cheaper. The café on the square is expensive, but the one on the corner is cheap.
b2-30-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how the two cafés differ.
cues: Say that the café on the square is expensive
Say that the café on the corner is cheap
b2-30-01.target: El café de la plaza es caro; el de la esquina, en cambio, es barato.
b2-30-01.english: The café on the square is expensive; the one on the corner, on the other hand, is cheap.
b2-30-01.canDo: I can use *en cambio* to set two different things side by side.

b2-30-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Not the Cinema
b2-30-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you went to the cinema on Saturday. You did not go to the cinema: you went to the theatre.
b2-30-02.prompt: Tell Meg where you did not go and where you went.
cues: Say that you did not go to the cinema
b2-30-02.target: No fui al cine, sino al teatro.
b2-30-02.english: I did not go to the cinema, but to the theatre.
b2-30-02.canDo: I can use *sino* and *sino que* after a negative to replace an idea.

b2-30-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Out in the Rain
b2-30-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if you went out in the rain yesterday. It was raining hard, but you went out all the same.
b2-30-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the weather was like and what you did anyway.
cues: Say that it was raining hard
Say that you went out all the same
b2-30-03.english: It was raining hard; even so, I went out.
b2-30-03.canDo: I can use *aun así* to say that something happens in spite of a difficulty.

b2-30-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Life in the Centre
b2-30-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think about living in the centre of Budapest. It is convenient, but it is also very noisy.
b2-30-04.prompt: Tell Meg the good point and the bad point of living in the centre.
cues: Say what is good about the centre
Say what is bad about it
b2-30-04.target: Por un lado, el centro es cómodo; por otro, es muy ruidoso.
b2-30-04.english: On the one hand, the centre is convenient; on the other, it is very noisy.
b2-30-04.canDo: I can use *por un lado … por otro* to weigh an advantage and a drawback.

b2-30-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book on Loan
b2-30-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks to borrow a book. You say yes, but he must bring it back on Monday.
b2-30-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that he can borrow the book, and on what condition.
cues: Say that you lend him the book
Say that he must return it on Monday
b2-30-05.target: Te presto el libro; eso sí, lo devuelves el lunes.
b2-30-05.english: I'll lend you the book; mind you, you give it back on Monday.
b2-30-05.canDo: I can use *eso sí* to accept something and add a condition.

b2-30-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Book about a War
b2-30-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you read about Euclides da Cunha. He was a newspaper correspondent in the war of Canudos, but he did not only write articles: he wrote a book about the war.
b2-30-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what Da Cunha did with what he saw, and contrast it with what a correspondent usually does.
cues: Say what a correspondent usually writes
Contrast it with what Da Cunha wrote
b2-30-consolidation.target: Un corresponsal suele escribir artículos; Da Cunha, en cambio, escribió un libro sobre la guerra de Canudos.
b2-30-consolidation.english: A correspondent usually writes articles; Da Cunha, on the other hand, wrote a book about the war of Canudos.
b2-30-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Euclides da Cunha and his book Los sertones.
